description: Compatibility fixtures for the browsing seam. Each fixture is one deliberate deviation from a message that would otherwise be accepted, and states the verdict a conforming decoder must reach. The kind of each fixture says which artifact reaches that verdict, so no row claims more than was run. Run them with: python3 taffy-core/contracts/browsing/codegen/generate.py --verify

verdicts.ACCEPT: The message is valid at this version and is accepted.
verdicts.REJECT_CLOSED_ENUM: A closed enumeration carries a value outside the members this version defines. The message is unsupported and fails closed; the value is never coerced to a known member.
verdicts.REJECT_MALFORMED: The message breaks a shape rule: a missing or extra field, a wrong scalar type, or a presence combination the contract forbids.
verdicts.REJECT_OVERSIZED: The message is otherwise valid and is refused only because it exceeds a bound the contract declares.
verdicts.REJECT_VERSION: The declared contract version is one this build does not speak, so the required meaning may have changed. The message is refused on the version alone.

kinds.enum: A committed document whose closed enumeration carries a value outside the contract. The generated Rust `from_wire` must answer that the value is unsupported.
kinds.bound: A committed document measured against the generated limit constant the product compiles in. The generated Rust constant must answer that the measurement is over.
kinds.version: A committed document at a declared contract version, answered against the version this build speaks.
kinds.record: A committed document answered by this contract's own shape rules in the generator. No shipped decoder runs; these records cross the seam as Mojo, and no Mojo decoder can be driven from a stdlib-only Python generator.
kinds.declaration: A committed schema fragment the schema validator must refuse. This is how a rule about what the contract may declare is executed rather than asserted.
kinds.unexecuted: A rule this contract does not express and nothing here can run. It carries a written reason and is never counted as covered.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed. A failure outside the set this version defines is unsupported and fails closed.
fixtures.deviation: A navigation carries a failure no member of NavigationFailure holds.
fixtures.note: NONE is the neighbour a lenient reader must never round to, and it is the one that reads as `the page loaded`. A surface that rounded here would let an assistant claim it read a page that never arrived, which is the exact failure this enumeration was written to prevent.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed, including which trusted surface is standing in front of the content.
fixtures.deviation: A navigation names an interstitial no member of InterstitialKind holds.
fixtures.note: OTHER already exists for an interstitial this build does not recognise, so an unknown wire value is not that case: it is a peer speaking a vocabulary this build does not have. Rounding it to NONE would tell a surface the page is showing when a security interstitial is.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed, including where a download has got to.
fixtures.deviation: A download carries a state no member of DownloadState holds.
fixtures.note: The state decides which commands a surface offers. COMPLETE is the neighbour that matters: offering `open` for a file whose bytes are not all there asks the platform to open something that does not exist yet.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed, including who a tab belongs to.
fixtures.deviation: A tab names an owner no member of TabOwner holds.
fixtures.note: UNKNOWN exists and means `treat it as the user's`, which is the strict answer. An unknown wire value must still refuse rather than fall into it, because falling into the strict answer silently is how a build stops noticing that its peer is describing a category it has never heard of.

fixtures.rule: Every collection is bounded, and the bound is the one the product compiles in.
fixtures.deviation: A measured tab count one past MAX_TABS.
fixtures.note: This row measures a count rather than carrying two hundred and fifty-seven tab records. The bound has to be checked from the length before an element is read, or a four-byte count reserves as much memory as it likes.

fixtures.rule: A host is bounded by MAX_HOST_BYTES, which is the longest a DNS name can be.
fixtures.deviation: A measured host length one byte past that bound.
fixtures.note: The bound is not a buffer size, it is a statement that the string is a host. Something longer is not a long host; it is something else, and a surface that drew it in an address bar would be drawing whatever it actually is.

fixtures.rule: A record carries every field this version declares. Absence is not a default.
fixtures.note: The tempting reading is that an absent status means zero, which this contract does define as `nothing committed`. That is exactly why absence may not mean it: a peer that forgot the field and a peer that committed nothing would become indistinguishable.

fixtures.rule: A scalar is the type the contract declares it to be.
fixtures.deviation: A download whose total size arrives as text.
fixtures.note: A reader that parsed it would be deciding what `4096` means — bytes, kilobytes, or a number some locale wrote differently — in a decoder. The field is a count of bytes and its type says so.

fixtures.rule: A different major version changes required meaning. The message is refused on the version alone, without inspecting the body.
fixtures.deviation: A tab declared at major version 2, carrying a body this version happens to understand completely.
fixtures.note: The body being readable is the point. A build that accepted it because nothing looked wrong would be speaking a version it does not have, and the first field whose meaning changed rather than whose shape did would pass unnoticed.

fixtures.rule: A higher minor version of the same major is additive. A reader accepts the message and ignores the fields it does not define.
fixtures.deviation: A navigation declared at the next minor version of this major, carrying one field this build does not define.
fixtures.note: Accepting is not the same as understanding. The surface draws the fields this build knows; the one it does not know is ignored, which is only safe because a minor step may not change what an existing field means. The declared version must stay one past this contract's minor: raised in the same change that raises the schema, or the fixture quietly becomes a past minor and stops testing the boundary it exists for.

fixtures.rule: This contract may not declare a field whose name carries an authority-bearing substring; raw_url and full_url are on that list.
fixtures.deviation: A tab record that hands a surface the whole location of the page it is showing.
fixtures.note: A host is what a person is shown and what a switcher needs. A full location is a credential-bearing string often enough that this seam refuses to be the thing that carries one — and a tab list is the most-copied record here, reaching every surface that draws a switcher.

fixtures.refusal: a record field cannot carry pending_remote
fixtures.rule: A record is a value. A field of one may not be a handle, however the interface it names is declared.
fixtures.deviation: A tab record that stores a connection to the surface's own observer.
fixtures.note: Snapshots here are whole, resent on every change, and copied on the way. A connection survives none of that, so the second snapshot would carry a field the first one closed.

fixtures.reason: The rule is that exactly one tab in a snapshot carries selected, and that the navigation describes that tab. It is a relation between two fields of two different records in one message, and this contract's shape rules describe records one at a time. Expressing it would need a cross-record presence rule the schema does not have; until that exists the browser-side projection is the only thing that can hold it, and browsing_projection_unittest.cc is where it is asserted.
fixtures.rule: A snapshot has exactly one selected tab, and the navigation it carries is that tab's.
fixtures.deviation: A snapshot whose navigation names a host no tab in its own list is on.
fixtures.note: Counted separately and never as covered. A surface that met this message would draw an address bar for a tab that is not in its own switcher, and nothing in this corpus would have refused it.
